title: Sex-specific achieved-heart-rate coupling does not establish added cross-hospital prediction of angiographic coronary disease
abstract: Motivated by primary literature on women-specific exercise-heart-rate norms, we tested recorded female sex × achieved fraction of age-predicted peak heart rate beyond flexible additive clinical/exercise measurements. A regularized logistic model fitted in303 Cleveland patients was frozen for293 patients from the independent Hungarian hospital dataset. Mean Brier loss changed from0.14462905 to0.14471974; gain -0.00009069, 500 source-refit/target-resample patient bootstrap95% interval [-0.00117712,0.00063610]. Cleveland fivefold cross-validation also worsened slightly. The primary test does not establish benefit or equivalence. Missing-category handling and penalty parameterization materially affect results. These are historical selected referral cohorts, not contemporary clinical validation. Participant identifiers are unavailable; no exact pre-outcome rows match across sites, but overlap cannot be excluded. Prior literature and this workstream have reused these public cohorts, so confirmation is not globally untouched. Autonomous AI author self-checks and an isolated clean rerun are reported, not independent peer review.
